set.descent_text: From the summit, rappel the southeast rib to the col between East Peak and the Gargoyle, then follow the long snow gully back down to the glacier.

review.notes: Descent only, single route page; rappel count omitted.

set.descent_text: Just below the top of the lower buttress the route merges with the original line. From the ledge system there you can descend on fixed anchors straight down the face of the lower buttress, left of this route, or carry on to the top of Ironman and use the fixed anchors from its summit down the upper buttress. Replace old webbing as needed.
set.approach: The Adamants are reached on foot from the east, from Fairy Meadows, or by helicopter. Slinky Tassle starts at the north end of the toe of Ironman's southwest buttress, at a thin left-leaning crack and flake a short way left of the original route.

review.notes: Route page for start and descent; Adamants area page for access.

set.approach: The wall is reached by a long logging-road drive on the Goat Lake main, then a flagged trail that starts across the D-Branch River and climbs through old-growth forest to the foot of Amon Rudh. Kolibri Crack is a splitter crack on the southeast face.

review.notes: Approach only; shared wall access from the area page and the Mormegil page. Route page says the top is a ledge below the summit but gives no descent.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route. Take extra webbing, and be careful not to rappel over the big roof.
set.approach: The wall is reached by a long logging-road drive on the Goat Lake main, then a flagged trail. After the bridge over the D-Branch River, the trail leaves on the right and climbs through old-growth forest, generally along the southwest ridge. Past large boulders the trail bears right (flagging that goes straight uphill is a false lead), then it crosses a big gully and reaches a camp, with the base of the wall in view just beyond. The Mormegil begins at the far west end of the wall, to the left of a huge roof, a short bushwhack from the trail.

review.notes: Route page for trail details and descent; area page confirms the Goat Lake main and the flagged trail on the far side of the river. Distances, rope length and road-access hours omitted.

set.descent_text: From the summit ridge, rappel the east face. The stations vary between pins and slung horns and shift from year to year, so carry slings and extra cord. The face is loose, rockfall is a real hazard, and ropes snag easily. Below the bergschrund a short downclimb leads onto the glacier, and from there the party walks back toward the Applebee camp.
set.approach: The usual way in is from the East Creek Basin camp. Hike up the ridge toward the middle tower and traverse a snow slope to the upper ridge overlooking the foot of the North Tower, then set rappels there to reach the glacier. Cross the cirque to the foot of the west face. Rockfall comes down both the rappels and the cirque from the face above, so move through quickly. Climbing begins on ledges over the glacier, at the point where the lower apron juts out farthest.

review.notes: East-face rappel descent agrees on two route pages; rappel counts differ (5-6 vs four) so none given. Approach from the route page, matched by the Seventh Rifle page on the East Creek rappels.

set.descent_text: Rappel the east face just below the summit, working down to the bergschrund, then downclimb a short way onto the glacier. The east face is loose, so move with care, and carry spare webbing to replace old anchors. From the glacier, walk back to the Applebee camp.
set.approach: The approach is from the East Creek Basin. A common plan is to bivy at the boulder below Middle Howser, then rappel the bolted anchors to reach the foot of the tower. The line begins left of the west face's lowest point, where a broad crack in a corner sits beside a splitter hand crack on the wall to its right.

review.notes: Route page; east-face rappel descent is confirmed independently on the Watchtower page. Rappel count omitted because pages disagree.

set.descent_text: The east face is the usual way off the tower. A rappel line has also been put in down the whole west face, following the route; the top anchors are at the spot where the scrambling along the ridge starts, close to where the routes at the left end of the wall finish.
set.approach: This route is on the west face of North Howser Tower. One approach is from the East Creek Basin by rappelling down to the glacier, which is strenuous; a longer alternative skirts the north side of the massif. The base is on the west face.

review.notes: Single route page. Row says 1 pitch / 5.9 A3 - pitch count looks wrong for a west-face route.

set.descent_text: From the top of the Minaret, either continue to the summit of South Howser and make the Beckey-Chouinard rappels, or rappel the route Doubting the Millennium. The latter is less casual than it sounds, and ropes stick easily on the aid sections.
set.approach: The Minaret is the granite tower that rises from the glacier in front of South Howser Tower, a short walk uphill from the East Creek bivy sites. The route starts up Bad Hair Day and stays on the Italian Pillar where Bad Hair Day goes right.

review.notes: Route page for descent and start; area page for the East Creek bivy access. Single source each.
